title: Document Runtime LTS channel, support window, and backport policy
author: Elliot Price
body:
## Summary
This PR adds customer-facing documentation for the Runtime LTS channel: what it is, who it’s for, how long it’s supported, what changes qualify for backport, and how to read the “slower-change” LTS release notes. It also adds Private deployment upgrade/rollback guidance links and clarifies version pinning semantics.

## Why
Enterprise Dedicated/Private customers have been asking for (a) a stable runtime baseline for 6–12+ months, (b) a predictable patch cadence, and (c) an explicit backport policy with a clear risk rubric. Support and Sales also need canonical language for “what LTS covers / doesn’t cover.”

This is the docs counterpart to the Runtime LTS branch work happening in the runtime repo and the first pilot preparations.

## What’s included
- New docs page: Runtime LTS channel overview
  - Definition: stability-focused runtime track intended for Dedicated + Private
  - Support window: 12 months standard, optional extension for contracted customers (wording aligned with Product)
  - Patch cadence: monthly patch releases; out-of-band security patches as needed
  - What’s not included: feature parity with mainline; experimental heuristics; non-critical refactors
- New docs page: Backport policy
  - Eligibility buckets: Security, Sev1 correctness/crash, Sev2 major degradation
  - Risk rubric: minimal diff preference, test requirements, perf validation gates
  - Approvals: Runtime + Release Eng + SRE; expedited path for security
  - Expectations: no “best effort” for feature requests; follow-on fixes may be deferred
- New docs page: Interpreting LTS release notes
  - Taxonomy used in LTS notes (Security, Reliability/Correctness, Performance/Latency, Ops/Packaging)
  - Required metadata: affected versions, known issues, mitigations, compatibility matrix pointers
  - Guidance on when to upgrade: mandatory vs recommended vs optional patches
- Upgrade/rollback guidance pointers
  - Links to Private installer pinning + checksum verification section
  - Rollback checklist + “validate after upgrade” steps
- Glossary and FAQ updates
  - “LTS vs latest” selection guidance
  - “How do I request a backport?” (routes to Support intake + required info)

## Customer-facing wording highlights
- LTS is a stability track. New features land on mainline first and may not be backported.
- Backports prioritize correctness, security, and high-severity reliability issues.
- LTS release notes are “slower-change” and include explicit known issues + mitigations.

## Files / structure
- docs/runtime/lts/overview.md (new)
- docs/runtime/lts/backport-policy.md (new)
- docs/runtime/lts/release-notes-guide.md (new)
- docs/private/upgrade/runtime-lts.md (new)
- docs/support/backport-requests.md (updated)
- docs/release-notes/lts-format.md (new)
- docs/_includes/compatibility-matrix-links.md (new)
- docs/glossary.md (updated)
- docs/faq/runtime-lts.md (new)
- mkdocs.yml (nav wiring)
- redirects.yml (new redirects for older “release channels” page)
- docs/images/runtime-lts-channel-console.png (added placeholder image; can be replaced with final Console screenshot)

## Notes / assumptions
- Support window and cadence are documented as policy targets; contract language remains the source of truth for specific customers.
- The page intentionally avoids specific branch names/tags in the primary intro (those are included in an “Advanced / pinning” section) to reduce churn if naming evolves.
- Private installation details reference pin-by-tag + checksum verification. Exact commands are aligned with current installer behavior but may require a follow-up once ENG-4827 fully lands.

## Validation
- Built docs site locally (mkdocs): navigation renders; links resolve
- Ran link checker: fixed 2 broken anchors

## Screenshots
- Added a placeholder Console UX image showing where customers will see “LTS” label + link to notes (pending final product UI)

review_conversation:
Connor O'Brien (2025-02-20): Can we be explicit that backports require perf gate sign-off and can be waived only with Release Eng + SRE approval? Also suggest adding examples for Sev1 vs Sev2.
Elliot Price (2025-02-20): Added perf gate requirement in the Backport Policy page and added a short “Examples” section with concrete symptoms + impact thresholds. Also added a waiver sentence requiring Release Eng + SRE sign-off.

Marissa Cole (2025-02-21): The support window section should avoid implying contractual guarantees. Please change “guaranteed 12 months” to “standard target support window is 12 months” and add a note about contract terms.
Elliot Price (2025-02-21): Updated language across all pages to “standard target support window” and added the contract disclaimer callout in the overview + FAQ.

Dev Patel (2025-02-24): The backport request section needs required fields (runtime version, model, repro, logs, business impact). Also please align severity mapping to Support’s Sev1/Sev2 definitions.
Elliot Price (2025-02-24): Updated Support intake page with a required-fields checklist and mapped it to Support severity definitions; added explicit example of ‘latency regression p95 +%’ as Sev2 candidate with perf evidence.

Dr. Aisha Rahman (2025-02-26): On security patches, we should avoid publishing a hard SLA in public docs. Recommend describing “expedited out-of-band security patches” and directing customers to security advisory channel.
Elliot Price (2025-02-26): Adjusted security section: removed concrete turnaround numbers, added language about expedited out-of-band patches and referencing security advisories / support channel.

Vivek Kulkarni (2025-03-02): Private upgrade page: please clarify rollback expectations (supported to previous LTS patch) and emphasize checksum verification for pinned images.
Elliot Price (2025-03-02): Added rollback guidance: ‘previous LTS patch within same LTS line’ and expanded checksum verification section with a short example + note to validate after upgrade.
